I am an old woman of eighty rains, and my legs are not as strong as before, but I still know the ways of the land that my mother taught me. This small plot of mine is only a corner of the earth, but it feeds me and my grandchildren, so I will tend it with the old ways. I have no money for those chemical fertilizers or sprays from the shop, and the rains in our land have always been enough for the yams and cassava if one plants at the right time. My family will help me clear and weed it by hand, and I will spread the ash and compost from our compound to make the soil sweet.
